source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Capella Playground (interactive SQL++/SDK tutorial execution environment)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a new member of the access-surface family (alongside capella:query-tab/data-api/cbsh), but with a materially different security model: it runs code in a remote sandboxed execution environment rather than proxying the user's own client, and auto-provisions/destroys its own ephemeral credential rather than using the user's cluster access credentials

concepts.label: Playground temporary credential (auto-generated, auto-destroyed)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a distinct, short-lived credential class from the standard cluster access credentials documented elsewhere (manage-database-users.md); worth its own concept since its lifecycle (generated per-run, destroyed after execution, network access revoked after 1 hour) is unlike any other credential type in the registry

relations.subject: capella:playground
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures 'this surface auto-issues and auto-revokes its own scoped credential per action', distinct from requiresCapellaRole (an actor-identity gate) and requiresSetting (a configuration dependency)
relations.evidence: Generates a temporary credential for you with read and write access to the bucket you used for the code example. This temporary credential is destroyed after your code example request is executed.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike capella:query-tab/data-api/cbsh (promoted as a family specifically because other pages state incompatibilities against them), this page states no incompatibility - the Playground is self-contained and doesn't claim to run against the user's real application code paths, so there's no 'feature X doesn't work via the Playground' claim to capture here. Not forced into the family's governing predicate.

cross_component_finding: The Playground is a genuinely new access surface not previously seen in this registry's capella:query-tab/data-api/cbsh family: it's a remote, network-firewalled, sandboxed execution environment (rather than a proxy for the user's own client) that mints and destroys its own scoped credential per run, and imposes runtime limits per language. This is a materially different security/access model from the rest of the family, worth flagging for the coordinator to decide whether it belongs in the same access-surface family or its own axis (an ephemeral-sandbox axis) given the credential-lifecycle difference.
